notes: The Jewish way of life, a word that first appears in Greek in the period of Maccabees and describes the commitment to Jewish practices and identity. In 1:13-14, Paul says that in his former "Judaism" he was advancing beyond many of his own age. It appears only here in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: My way of living in time past in the Jews' religion.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To take out, pull out, or rescue (ex "out" plus haireō "to take"). In 1:4, Christ gave himself "that he might deliver us out of this present evil age." It is also used for Peter's rescue in Acts 12:11.

elsewhere.note: He delivered him out of all his afflictions.
The Lord has sent out his angel and delivered me.
I came with the soldiers and rescued him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Evil, bad, harmful. In 1:4 the present age is "evil." It is also used for "the evil one" (Matthew 13:19; Ephesians 6:16).

elsewhere.note: He makes his sun rise on the evil and the good.
Deliver us from the evil one.
So that you may be able to withstand in the evil day.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To turn to the opposite, to change, to twist. In 1:7, "some want to pervert the Good News of Christ," turning it into something else.

elsewhere.note: The sun will be turned into darkness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To move from one place or position to another, to transfer, and so to switch loyalty. In 1:6, "you are so quickly deserting him who called you," literally "changing sides."

elsewhere.note: They were brought over to Shechem.
The priesthood being changed.
Turning the grace of our God into sensuality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To convince, win over, or trust (the passive means "be persuaded, obey"). In 1:10, "Am I now persuading men, or God?" In 3:1 and 5:7 the same word describes what people have stopped obeying.

elsewhere.note: Some of them were persuaded.
I am persuaded that neither death nor life.
Obey your leaders.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To chase, pursue, or persecute. In 1:13 and 1:23, Paul says he persecuted the church of God; in Philippians 3:12 he pursues the goal of knowing Christ.

elsewhere.note: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake.
Why do you persecute me?
Pursue hospitality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To sack a city, to ravage or destroy. In 1:13 and 1:23, Paul says he "was destroying" the church. In Acts 9:21 the same word describes how those in Damascus saw Paul before.

elsewhere.note: Isn't this he who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who called on this name?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to visit and get to know
notes: To learn by inquiry, to visit a person or place in order to get acquainted (from which we get "history"). In 1:18, Paul went to Jerusalem "to get to know Cephas." It appears only here in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To act as a hypocrite along with others, to play a part together. In 2:13, "the rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy," even Barnabas, when Peter withdrew from the Gentile believers.

elsewhere.note: The rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To pull back, to withdraw (as a sailor lowers a sail), often out of fear. In 2:12, Peter "drew back and separated himself" from the Gentile believers when the men from James came.

elsewhere.note: I didn't shrink from declaring to you anything profitable.
If he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To make someone a slave completely (kata "down" plus doulos "slave"). In 2:4, the "false brothers" wanted "to bring us into bondage," and in 2 Corinthians 11:20 Paul says the Corinthians put up with those who "enslave" them.

elsewhere.note: You bear with it if a man enslaves you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A person who claims to be a fellow believer but is not (pseudēs "false" plus adelphos "brother"). In 2:4 Paul speaks of "false brothers secretly brought in" to spy on the freedom believers have.

elsewhere.note: Perils among false brothers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Brought in by stealth, sneaked in (para "alongside" plus eis "into" plus agō "lead"). In 2:4 the false brothers were "secretly brought in" to spy. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Because of the false brothers secretly brought in.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A column or pillar. In 2:9, James, Cephas, and John "seemed to be pillars" of the Jerusalem church. In 1 Timothy 3:15 the church is the "pillar and ground of the truth."

elsewhere.note: The pillar and ground of the truth.
I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God.
His feet like pillars of fire.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The right side or right hand, the hand of honor and power. In 2:9, the pillars gave Paul and Barnabas "the right hand of fellowship," a handshake of partnership.

elsewhere.note: If your right eye causes you to stumble.
Sat down at the right hand of God.
He is at my right hand.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To judge against someone, to find fault. In 2:11, Paul opposed Peter because "he stood condemned," that is, his behavior was self-evidently wrong. It is also used in 1 John 3:20-21 for the heart condemning us.

elsewhere.note: If our heart condemns us.
If our heart doesn't condemn us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To adopt Jewish customs. In 2:14, Paul asks Peter, "how can you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?" It is the origin of the later word "Judaizers" for those who pressed Gentile believers to adopt Jewish practices. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: How can you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The state of being uncircumcised, used for Gentiles as a group ("the uncircumcision"). In 2:7, Paul has been entrusted with "the gospel of the uncircumcision," as Peter with "the circumcision."

elsewhere.note: If you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The gospel, good news. Paul accuses the Galatians of turning to "a different good news, which is not another" (1:6-9), and says his gospel came by revelation, not from a person (1:11-12).

range.note: News of a king's triumph or accession.
The message about Jesus, later also a name for books like Mark.

elsewhere.note: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
The gospel I preached to you.
The gospel that was preached by me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Something under a curse. "Let him be accursed" if anyone preaches a different gospel (1:8-9), even an angel; the same word closes 1 Corinthians (16:22).

elsewhere.note: I would wish to be accursed and cut off from Christ.
Let him be accursed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Revelation, an uncovering. "It came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ" (1:12), and God "was pleased to reveal his Son in me" (1:15-16).

elsewhere.note: According to the revelation of the mystery.
Through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
The revelation of Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An age. "This present evil age" (1:4) from which Christ rescues us.

elsewhere.note: "The harvest is the end of the age."
"The end of the age."
"In the ages to come."
Through whom he made the ages.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A zealot, an eager person. Paul was "more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of my fathers" (1:14).

range.note: A member of the resistance movement.

elsewhere.note: Being zealous for God as all of you are this day.
Zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
A people for his own possession who are zealous for good works.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A tradition, something handed down. Paul had been very zealous for the "traditions of my fathers" (1:14).

range.note: The Pharisees' accumulated rulings on living out the law.

elsewhere.note: The same dispute, in Matthew.
Paul, zealous for the traditions of his ancestors.
Paul praises them for holding to the traditions.
"Hold to the traditions you were taught."

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To set apart. God "set me apart, even from my mother's womb" (1:15).

elsewhere.note: Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul.
Who set me apart before I was born.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One sent out, an apostle. Paul begins by insisting he is "an apostle, not from men" (1:1, 1:17, 1:19).

range.note: Someone sent to act with the sender's authority.
The twelve, and later others such as Paul.

elsewhere.note: Whom he also named apostles.
Numbered with the eleven apostles.
Then to all the apostles.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Grace, favor. Paul stresses that God called him "by his grace" (1:15), that the Galatians were called "in the grace of Christ" (1:6), and says "I don't make void the grace of God" (2:21).

elsewhere.note: The Word was full of grace and truth.
The gospel of the grace of God.
By grace you are saved.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Peace. "Grace to you and peace" (1:3), and the letter ends with peace and mercy (6:16).

elsewhere.note: "Peace to you."
My peace I give to you.
The peace of God that surpasses understanding.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A gathering, a church. "The assemblies of Galatia" (1:2), and the "assembly of God" Paul once persecuted (1:13).

range.note: A city's gathering of free citizens.
God's gathered people in the Greek Old Testament.

elsewhere.note: I will build my church.
To the church of God that is in Corinth.
The church, which is his body.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sharing, partnership. "The right hand of fellowship" (2:9) is a handshake of partnership between Paul, Barnabas, and the pillars.

elsewhere.note: The fellowship.
The favor of taking part in the relief of the saints.
Your partnership in the gospel.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Poor. "They asked only that we should remember the poor" (2:10), which Paul was eager to do.

elsewhere.note: The poor have good news preached to them.
Give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven.
God chose those who are poor in the world.
Remember the poor.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Circumcision. "The gospel of the circumcision" was entrusted to Peter (2:7-9), and Peter drew back for fear of "those of the circumcision" (2:12).

elsewhere.note: The circumcision party criticized Peter.
In Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts.
We are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To declare righteous, to justify. "A man is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ" (2:16-17); the word is central in the letter.

elsewhere.note: This man went down to his house justified.
Not justified by works of the law.
Justified by his grace.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A deed, a work. "By the works of the law no flesh will be justified" (2:16).

elsewhere.note: Let them see your good works.
Created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.
I am doing a work in your days.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Law, especially the law of Moses. The word appears more than thirty times in Galatians, beginning with "not justified by the works of the law" (2:16, 2:19, 2:21).

elsewhere.note: I have not come to abolish the Law but to fulfill it.
The law was given through Moses.
The law was our guardian until Christ came.
Whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Faith, trust. "Through faith in Jesus Christ" (2:16) or "the faithfulness of Jesus Christ"; "I live by faith in the Son of God" (2:20).

range.note: Confidence in a person or what they can do.
Being trustworthy and loyal (STEPBible tags this sense separately).

elsewhere.note: Your faith has made you well.
By grace you have been saved through faith.
Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To crucify. "I have been crucified with Christ" (2:19-20).

range.note: Put to death on a cross.

elsewhere.note: "Let him be crucified!"
"Crucify, crucify him!"
This Jesus whom you crucified.
We preach Christ crucified.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To live. "It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me" (2:20).

elsewhere.note: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father.
The righteous shall live by faith.
Serve the living and true God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sin. "Is Christ a servant of sin?" (2:17) and Paul's insistence that Christ gave himself "for our sins" (1:4).

range.note: A wrong against God or others.

elsewhere.note: He will save his people from their sins.
The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
If we confess our sins.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To love. "The Son of God, who loved me" (2:20).

range.note: Care for another that shows itself in action.

elsewhere.note: Love your enemies.
Love one another as I have loved you.
We love because he first loved us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To hand over. "Who loved me and gave himself up for me" (2:20).

range.note: Pass something on, as a teaching.

elsewhere.note: God gave them up to uncleanness.
Whom I delivered to Satan, that they might learn not to blaspheme.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Freedom, liberty. "Our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus" (2:4); "for freedom Christ has set us free" (5:1); "you were called to freedom" (5:13).

elsewhere.note: The glorious liberty of the children of God.
For freedom Christ has set us free.
Why is my liberty judged by another's conscience?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Without understanding or good sense (a- "not" plus noeō "to think"), not a harsh insult but a sharp one. Paul calls the Galatians "foolish" for turning back (3:1, 3:3).

elsewhere.note: You foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe.
I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish.
Many foolish and harmful lusts.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to bewitch, to cast an evil eye
notes: To put a spell on someone or cast the evil eye, often out of envy. In 3:1, Paul asks, "who has bewitched you?" using a picture of magic to describe how unaccountably they have turned from the cross. It appears only here in the New Testament.

elsewhere.note: Who has bewitched you?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to write before, to portray publicly
notes: To write beforehand, or to post publicly like a notice. In 3:1, Jesus Christ was "openly displayed as crucified" before their eyes, as if on a public poster. In Romans 15:4 it means "written before."

elsewhere.note: Whatever things were written before were written for our learning.
As I wrote before in brief.
Who were long ago marked out for this condemnation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The act of hearing, or what is heard, a report or message. In 3:2 and 3:5, Paul asks if they received the Spirit by works of the law or "by the hearing of faith," meaning hearing the message and believing it.

elsewhere.note: Who has believed our report?
So faith comes by hearing.
The report of him went out into all Syria.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Seed, or the offspring it grows into. In 3:16 Paul notes that the promise was made to Abraham and to his "seed" (singular), which he says is Christ; in 3:29 all who belong to Christ are "Abraham's seed."

elsewhere.note: The promise to Abraham or to his seed.
Not because they are Abraham's seed are they all children.
Are they Abraham's seed? So am I.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To speak well of, to bless. In 3:8-9, God said to Abraham, "all the nations will be blessed in you," and those who believe are blessed along with Abraham.

elsewhere.note: In you all the families of the earth will be blessed (LXX).
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Bless those who curse you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A curse, a call for harm. In 3:10-13, those who rely on the works of the law are "under a curse," because the law curses those who do not keep it, and Christ redeems us by "becoming a curse for us."

elsewhere.note: Its end is to be burned.
Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing.
Children of cursing.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Under a curse, in the language of Deuteronomy 27:26 and 21:23. In 3:10 Paul quotes Deuteronomy: "Cursed is everyone who doesn't continue in all things written," and in 3:13 "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree."

elsewhere.note: Cursed is everyone who doesn't continue in all things written in the book of the law.
Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To buy out of slavery, to ransom (ex "out of" plus agorazō "to buy"). In 3:13, "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law," and in 4:5, he redeems those under the law so that they can receive adoption.

elsewhere.note: Redeeming the time.
Redeeming the time.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To make legally binding, to ratify. In 3:15, "even though it is only a man's covenant, yet when it has been confirmed, no one annuls it or adds to it," which Paul uses to say that God's covenant with Abraham cannot be changed by the law. The related word is used for a confirmed will.

elsewhere.note: I beg you to confirm your love toward him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A trusted slave who looked after a boy, taking him to and from school and supervising his behavior until he reached adulthood. The word is the root of "pedagogy," but a paidagōgos was a guardian, not a teacher. In 3:24-25, the law was our "guardian" until Christ came.

range.note: One who keeps a child in line.

elsewhere.note: You have ten thousand tutors in Christ, but not many fathers.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to shut up together, to confine
notes: To enclose, as fish in a net or prisoners in a cell. In 3:22-23, "the Scripture imprisoned all things under sin," and "we were held in custody under the law." In Romans 11:32 God "has shut up all in disobedience that he might have mercy on all."

elsewhere.note: They enclosed a great multitude of fish.
God has shut up all in disobedience.
Before faith came, we were kept in custody under the law.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to guard, to keep in custody
notes: To guard, as a garrison guards a city or a guard holds prisoners. In 3:23, "we were kept in custody under the law, imprisoned until the faith that was to come would be revealed."

elsewhere.note: The governor guarded the city of the Damascenes.
The peace of God will guard your hearts.
Who by the power of God are guarded through faith.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to put on, to clothe oneself
notes: To put on clothing, and so to take on a character or role. In 3:27, "as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ." Paul uses the picture often: "put on the Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 13:14).

elsewhere.note: Put on the Lord Jesus Christ.
Put on the new man.
Put on a heart of compassion.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One who receives an inheritance. In 3:29 and 4:1-7, those who belong to Christ are "Abraham's offspring and heirs according to promise," and "heirs of God through Christ."

elsewhere.note: If children, then heirs; heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ.
Whom he appointed heir of all things.
Heirs of the kingdom.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A son, or a male child. In Galatians Paul speaks of Christ as God's Son (1:16; 2:20; 4:4-6) and of believers as "sons of God through faith" (3:26; 4:6-7), with the legal sense of heirs in a Roman household.

range.note: One who inherits his father's place.

elsewhere.note: As many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
This is my beloved Son.
He has spoken to us in his Son.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One entrusted with the care of someone, a guardian of a minor, or a steward of an estate. In 4:2, an heir who is still a child is "under guardians and stewards" until the day his father set. It is used for Herod's steward in Luke 8:3.

range.note: One who looks after a minor.

elsewhere.note: The lord of the vineyard said to his steward.
Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A basic element, such as the letters of the alphabet, the elements of the world (earth, air, fire, water), or the elementary teaching of a subject. In 4:3 and 4:9, believers were enslaved to the "elementary principles of the world," which Paul calls "weak and beggarly." The sense is debated: basic religious teaching, cosmic powers, or both.

range.note: Spiritual forces thought to rule the world.

elsewhere.note: According to the elementary principles of the world.
If you died with Christ from the elementary principles of the world.
The first principles of the oracles of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to send out, to send away
notes: To send out with a mission (ex "out" plus apostellō "to send"). In 4:4 and 4:6, God "sent out" his Son, and then "sent out" the Spirit of his Son into believers' hearts.

elsewhere.note: The rich he has sent away empty.
Sent out our fathers the first time.
They sent him off to Tarsus.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Without strength, weak or ill. In 4:9, the "basic principles" are "weak and beggarly," unable to give life; in 1 Corinthians 1:25 God's weakness is stronger than people.

elsewhere.note: The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
God chose the weak things of the world.
A setting aside of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to labor, to toil, to grow weary
notes: To work hard until tired. In 4:11, Paul fears he has "labored over you in vain," and in 1 Corinthians 15:10, "I labored more abundantly than they all."

elsewhere.note: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened.
I labored more abundantly than they all.
That I didn't labor in vain.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To give shape or form to something (from morphē, "form"). In 4:19, Paul labors "until Christ is formed in you," using the picture of a mother giving birth. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Until Christ is formed in you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be in labor, to travail
notes: To suffer birth pains. In 4:19, Paul is "again in travail" for the Galatians until Christ is formed in them, and in 4:27 the passage from Isaiah speaks of a woman who "doesn't travail."

elsewhere.note: Cry aloud, you who have not been in labor (LXX).
Crying out in her pain to give birth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To say one thing and mean another, from which we get "allegory." In 4:24, Paul says the story of Hagar and Sarah "contains an allegory," that is, the women represent two covenants. It appears only here.

range.note: Read a story as a picture.

elsewhere.note: These things contain an allegory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A young female slave. In 4:22-31, Hagar is "the servant" (the slave woman), and Sarah is "the free woman." The same word is used for the girl who recognized Peter (Mark 14:66).

elsewhere.note: A maid came to him.
Beat the menservants and the maidservants.
A maid named Rhoda came to answer.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to throw out, to cast out
notes: To throw out or send away, with some force. In 4:30, quoting Genesis 21:10, "cast out the servant and her son." It is also the word for Jesus casting out demons and driving the sellers from the temple.

elsewhere.note: Jesus entered into the temple and drove out all of those who sold and bought.
He cast out many demons.
Him who comes to me I will in no way throw out.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The state of being a slave. In 4:24-25 Hagar "bears children into slavery," and in 5:1 Paul says "don't be entangled again with a yoke of bondage."

elsewhere.note: You didn't receive the spirit of bondage again to fear.
Delivered from the bondage of corruption.
Subject to bondage all their lives.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A specific time, opportunity, or season (distinct from chronos, general time). In 4:10 it describes the "seasons" the Galatians have begun to observe; in 6:9-10 it is the "due season" of harvest and the "opportunity" to do good.

elsewhere.note: The time is fulfilled.
Knowing the time, that it is already the hour.
Redeeming the time.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Spirit. The Galatians received the Spirit by faith, not by works (3:2-5, 3:14); God sent "the Spirit of his Son into your hearts" (4:6); Isaac was born "according to the Spirit" (4:29).

range.note: The Holy Spirit, or a spirit being.
Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
Receive the Holy Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To complete, to finish. "Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being perfected in the flesh?" (3:3).

elsewhere.note: When I have completed this, and have sealed to them this fruit.
He who began a good work will complete it.
They serve a copy.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To believe. "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness" (3:6); Scripture "imprisoned all things under sin so that the promise by faith... might be given to those who believe" (3:22).

elsewhere.note: Repent, and believe in the gospel.
Believe in the Lord Jesus.
If you believe in your heart.
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A promise. "The promise of the Spirit through faith" (3:14), the promises made to Abraham (3:16-22, 3:29), and "children of promise" (4:23, 4:28).

elsewhere.note: I am sending the promise of my Father upon you.
He has received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit.
The promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring.
Imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A covenant. "Even though it is only a man's covenant" (3:15-17), and "these are two covenants" (4:24).

range.note: An agreement God makes with his people.
A document that gives an inheritance.

elsewhere.note: The blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
This cup is the new covenant in my blood.
The new covenant.
The mediator of a new covenant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To baptize. "As many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ" (3:27).

elsewhere.note: Jesus comes to John to be baptized.
Jesus is baptized in the Jordan.
Be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Free. "There is neither bondservant nor free man" (3:28); "the free woman" (4:22-31).

elsewhere.note: There is neither slave nor free.
The Jerusalem above is free.
Free and slave, small and great.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A slave. "There is neither bondservant nor free" (3:28); "you are no longer a bondservant, but a son" (4:7).

range.note: A title of honor for those who serve the Lord.

elsewhere.note: Whoever wishes to be first among you must be your slave.
I would not be a servant of Christ.
Taking the form of a servant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One. "You are all one in Christ Jesus" (3:28); "not 'to seeds,' as of many, but as of one" (3:16).

elsewhere.note: The two shall become one flesh.
The Lord our God, the Lord is one.
You are all one in Christ Jesus.
There is one body and one Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An infant, a child. "As long as the heir is a child" (4:1) and "we, when we were children" (4:3).

elsewhere.note: You have revealed them to infants.
No longer children, tossed to and fro.
Everyone who partakes of milk is an infant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A steward, a household manager. "Under guardians and stewards until the day appointed by the father" (4:2).

range.note: Keeper of funds, as with Erastus.

elsewhere.note: Who then is the faithful and wise steward?
An overseer must be blameless, as God's steward.
Good stewards of God's varied grace.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Fullness. "When the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son" (4:4).

elsewhere.note: The patch tears away from the garment.
They took up twelve baskets full.
From his fullness we have all received.
When the fullness of time had come.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Adoption as a son. "That we might receive the adoption as children" (4:5).

range.note: Legal acceptance as a child and heir.

elsewhere.note: To them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants.
So that we might receive adoption as sons.
He predestined us for adoption as sons.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Father, an Aramaic word of close address. "Crying, Abba! Father!" (4:6).

range.note: A child's and an adult's word for father.

elsewhere.note: Abba, Father, all things are possible to you.
The Spirit cries, "Abba! Father!"

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A test, a trial. "That which was a trial to you in my flesh" (4:14).

elsewhere.note: Do not lead us into temptation.
No temptation has taken you but such as is common.
Count it all joy when you meet trials.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Flesh, human nature. "Born according to the flesh" (4:23, 4:29); the flesh is a major theme in chapters 5 and 6.

elsewhere.note: Those who live according to the flesh.
The flesh lusts against the Spirit.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to fall off, to fall away
notes: To fall out of something or off a position. In 5:4, those who want to be justified by the law have "fallen away from grace." It also describes a ship drifting (Acts 27:17) and flowers dropping their petals (James 1:11).

elsewhere.note: His chains fell off from his hands.
They would be cast ashore.
Its flower falls.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to hinder, to cut in on
notes: To block or impede, as of breaking up a road or cutting in on a runner. In 5:7, "you were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?"

elsewhere.note: I was hindered many times from coming to you.
Satan hindered us.
So that your prayers may not be hindered.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To desire strongly, for good or ill. In 5:17, "the flesh desires against the Spirit," and the Spirit against the flesh; the noun epithymia is "desire" or "lust."

elsewhere.note: Anyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her.
I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you.
I wouldn't have known coveting unless the law had said, You shall not covet.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Idol worship (eidōlon "idol" plus latreia "service"). In 5:20 it is in the list of the works of the flesh. In 1 Corinthians 10:14 Paul tells believers to "flee from idolatry."

range.note: Giving to something what belongs to God.

elsewhere.note: Flee from idolatry.
Covetousness, which is idolatry.
Abominable idolatries.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Use of drugs, potions, or magic, from which we get "pharmacy." In 5:20 it is in the list of the works of the flesh, and in Revelation it is linked to those excluded from the new Jerusalem.

elsewhere.note: With your sorcery all the nations were deceived.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Hatred, enmity, being on opposite sides. In 5:20 it is a work of the flesh. In Ephesians 2:14-16, Christ destroys the "enmity" between Jew and Gentile.

elsewhere.note: The mind of the flesh is hostile toward God.
Having killed the hostility through the cross.
Friendship with the world is hostility toward God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A standing apart (dicha "in two" plus stasis "standing"), division within a group. In 5:20 it is a work of the flesh, and in Romans 16:17 Paul warns about those who cause divisions.

elsewhere.note: Look out for those who are causing the divisions.
Jealousy and strife and divisions among you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Resentment at another's good fortune. In 5:21 it is a work of the flesh, and in Philippians 1:15 some preach Christ out of envy.

elsewhere.note: He knew that because of envy they had delivered him up.
Full of envy.
Living in malice and envy.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A noisy, drunken party with revelry. In 5:21 it is a work of the flesh, and in Romans 13:13 Paul says to walk honorably, not "in carousing and drunkenness."

elsewhere.note: Not in carousing and drunkenness.
Carousing, drinking parties.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Patience with people, a long fuse (the noun form of makrothymeō). In 5:22 it is part of the fruit of the Spirit, and Paul says that God shows it toward sinners (Romans 2:4).

elsewhere.note: The riches of his kindness and patience.
Humility, gentleness, patience.
With all patience and teaching.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A quality of moral goodness, benevolence in action. In 5:22 it is part of the fruit of the Spirit, and in Romans 15:14 Paul says the Roman believers are "full of goodness."

elsewhere.note: You yourselves also are full of goodness.
The fruit of the light is in all goodness.
Every desire of goodness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to walk in line, to follow
notes: To stand in a row, to march in line, and so to conduct oneself according to a rule. In 5:25 Paul says, "if we live by the Spirit, let's also keep in step with the Spirit," and in 6:16, "as many as walk by this rule."

elsewhere.note: You yourself also walk keeping the law.
Walk in the steps of the faith of our father Abraham.
Let's walk by the same rule.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Having an empty (kenos) opinion of oneself, wanting glory (doxa) for nothing. In 5:26, "let's not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another." It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Let's not become conceited, provoking one another.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To call out, challenge, or provoke to a contest. In 5:26 Paul warns against "provoking one another" in a church competing for status. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Provoking one another, envying one another.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To envy, to feel resentment at another's blessing. In 5:26, "envying one another," the verb form of phthonos. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Envying one another.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A fall to the side, a slip or wrongdoing (para "beside" plus piptō "to fall"). In 6:1, "if a man is caught in some wrongdoing." In Romans 5 Paul uses it for Adam's trespass.

elsewhere.note: If you forgive men their trespasses.
The free gift is not like the trespass.
Dead through your trespasses and sins.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A heavy weight, a burden. In 6:2, "bear one another's burdens." It is the same word Paul uses of the "weight of glory" in 2 Corinthians 4:17, and of the burden of apostolic authority in 1 Thessalonians 2:6.

elsewhere.note: We have borne the burden of the day.
To lay no greater burden on you.
I put no other burden on you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A load that someone carries, like a soldier's pack. In 6:5, "each one will bear his own load." Jesus uses the same word for his burden, which is "light" (Matthew 11:30).

elsewhere.note: My burden is light.
They bind heavy burdens.
You load men with burdens difficult to carry.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To fill up completely, to fulfill. In 6:2, "bear one another's burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ." In 1 Thessalonians 2:16 it is used of filling up sin to its limit.

elsewhere.note: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled.
The one who fills the place of the unlearned.
To supply what was lacking.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To deceive the mind (phrēn "mind" plus apataō "to deceive"). In 6:3, "if anyone thinks himself to be something when he is nothing, he deceives himself." It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: He deceives himself.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To work, do, or perform. In 6:10, "as we have opportunity, let's do what is good toward all," which sums up the practical teaching of the letter.

elsewhere.note: Son, go work today in the vineyard.
What must we do?
Rather let him labor, working with his hands.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Belonging to a house or household, a relative. In 6:10, Paul speaks of "the household of faith," the family of believers. It is also used in Ephesians 2:19 ("members of God's household") and 1 Timothy 5:8.

elsewhere.note: You are fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God.
If anyone doesn't provide for his own, specially his own household.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To make a fine appearance (eu "good" plus prosōpon "face"). In 6:12, "those who desire to make a good impression in the flesh" try to force circumcision. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: As many as desire to make a good impression in the flesh.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A mark made on the body, such as a brand on a slave or an animal, or a scar. In 6:17, "I bear on my body the marks of Jesus," probably the scars from beatings and stoning (2 Corinthians 11:23-25), showing he belongs to Christ.

elsewhere.note: I bear in my body the marks of Jesus.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A yoke, used of a burden of service. "Don't be entangled again with a yoke of bondage" (5:1); Jesus said his yoke is easy (Matthew 11:30).

range.note: Obligations someone places on you, like slavery or a law.

elsewhere.note: Take my yoke upon you.
Do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
Those who are under a yoke as bondservants.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to abolish, to bring to nothing
notes: To bring to nothing. "You are alienated from Christ" (5:4) and "then the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished" (5:11).

elsewhere.note: Do we then nullify the law through faith?
Our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death.
That through death he might destroy him who had the power of death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to work, to be at work
notes: To work, to be at work. "Faith working through love" (5:6).

elsewhere.note: He who supplies the Spirit and works miracles among you.
It is God who works in you.
Him who works all things after the counsel of his will.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Love. "Faith working through love" (5:6), "through love be servants" (5:13), "you shall love your neighbor" (5:14), and the first fruit of the Spirit (5:22).

elsewhere.note: As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you.
Faith, hope, and love abide, but the greatest of these is love.
The fruit of the Spirit is love.
God is love.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Yeast. "A little yeast leavens the whole lump" (5:9), a warning about the agitators' influence.

elsewhere.note: Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees.
The kingdom is like yeast a woman hid in flour.
A little yeast leavens the whole lump.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A stumbling block. "The stumbling block of the cross" (5:11).

range.note: The part of a trap that snaps shut.
Something that makes a person fall.

elsewhere.note: I lay in Zion a stumbling stone.
Then the offense of the cross has been removed.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Desire, lust. "You won't fulfill the lust of the flesh" (5:16) and those who belong to Christ "have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts" (5:24).

elsewhere.note: The desires for other things enter in.
I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you.
You will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
Not conforming to the passions of your former ignorance.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sexual immorality. The first of the works of the flesh (5:19).

range.note: The earliest sense, from the word for a prostitute.
As in Leviticus 18, which Acts 15 echoes.

elsewhere.note: From the heart come sexual immorality.
Abstain from sexual immorality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Impurity. "Uncleanness" (5:19).

elsewhere.note: God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness.
Sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness.
God did not call us to uncleanness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sensuality. "Lustfulness" (5:19).

elsewhere.note: Not in reveling and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and sensuality.
Sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness.
Living in sensuality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Strife. "Strife" (5:20), one of the works of the flesh.

elsewhere.note: Full of envy, murder, strife, deceit.
Strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger.
Some preach Christ even from envy and strife.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Jealousy. "Jealousy" (5:20).

elsewhere.note: Zeal for your house will consume me.
Filled with jealousy.
Your zeal for me.
As to zeal, a persecutor of the church.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Anger, passion. "Outbursts of anger" (5:20).

elsewhere.note: All were filled with anger in the synagogue.
Anger, wrath, malice.
The wine of the wrath of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Selfish ambition, rivalry. "Rivalries" (5:20).

elsewhere.note: To those who are self-seeking.
Strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries.
Do nothing from selfishness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A party, faction. "Factions" (5:20).

elsewhere.note: There must be factions among you.
Fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions.
False teachers who will secretly bring in destructive heresies.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Fruit. "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace..." (5:22).

elsewhere.note: You will know them by their fruits.
Produce fruits worthy of repentance.
The fruit of the Spirit.
Wisdom from above is full of good fruits.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Joy. "Joy," part of the fruit of the Spirit (5:22).

elsewhere.note: They rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.
For the joy set before him he endured the cross.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Kindness. "Kindness," part of the fruit (5:22).

elsewhere.note: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness.
The immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us.
Put on compassionate hearts, kindness.
When the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Self-control. The last of the fruit of the Spirit (5:23).

elsewhere.note: Gentleness, self-control.
Knowledge with self-control.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to restore, to mend, to put in order
notes: To restore, to mend. "Restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness" (6:1).

elsewhere.note: Mending their nets.
Restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness.
Will himself perfect, establish, strengthen you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To test. "Let each man test his own work" (6:4).

elsewhere.note: So that you may prove what is the will of God.
Test all things; hold fast to what is good.
The testing of your faith, more precious than gold.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To sow. "Whatever a man sows, that he will also reap" (6:7-8).

elsewhere.note: A sower went out to sow.
Whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.
If we sowed to you spiritual things.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To reap. "We will reap, if we don't give up" (6:7-9).

elsewhere.note: They don't sow, nor reap.
He will also reap.
He who reaps receives wages.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Decay, corruption. "From the flesh reap corruption" (6:8).

elsewhere.note: Delivered from the bondage of corruption.
He who sows to his own flesh will reap corruption.
Having escaped from the corruption that is in the world.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to lose heart, to give up
notes: To lose heart. "Let's not be weary in doing good" (6:9).

elsewhere.note: Always to pray and not to give up.
Let's not be weary in doing good.
I ask that you do not lose heart at my afflictions.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The world. "The world has been crucified to me, and I to the world" (6:14).

elsewhere.note: God so loved the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: New. "A new creation" (6:15).

elsewhere.note: I will drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.
The new covenant in my blood.
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
A new heaven and a new earth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Creation. "A new creation" (6:15).

elsewhere.note: The creation waits for the revealing of the children of God.
A new creation.
The firstborn of all creation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A rule, a standard. "As many as walk by this rule" (6:16).

elsewhere.note: As many as walk by this rule, peace be on them.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Mercy. "Peace and mercy be on them" (6:16).

range.note: Acting to help the one in need.
God's faithful kindness to his people.

elsewhere.note: Jesus quotes Hosea 6:6 again.
Justice, mercy, and faithfulness.
Mary: his mercy for those who fear him.
Mercy triumphs over judgment.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The cross. "The offense of the cross" (5:11; 6:12), and "far be it from me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ" (6:14).

range.note: The wooden frame used for crucifixion.
A picture of giving up one's life.

elsewhere.note: They compelled Simon to carry his cross.
Boast only in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.
